# What two layers need to be modified when migrating legged_control to a custom legged robot?

> **Current answer:** The hardware layer inherits from LeggedHW and implements read() and write() functions; the model layer follows legged_unitree_description to generate xacro/URDF files and adheres to joint/link naming conventions. This allows platform differences to be consolidated at the hardware interface and model description, without affecting the NMPC/WBC core.

## Problem and symptoms

- What is the minimum compatibility boundary when migrating legged_control to a custom legged robot?
- Why can't simulation controller and real controller be mixed?
- Direct modification of the main repository makes hardware compatibility hard to maintain.
- Real hardware starting cheater controller or running Gazebo on board causes incorrect state or resource risks.

## Environment

- ROS/ros-control; OCS2; A1; author uses a 11th-gen NUC, NMPC frequency close to 200 Hz; repository currently marked as no longer maintained.

## Priority diagnostics

- Check the hardware interface, description file, controller, and state estimator against the official repository directory.

## Possible causes

- Hardware read/write interface and joint naming do not meet framework assumptions.
- Using simulation truth state or simulation load on real hardware.

## Attempts

- Inherit LeggedHW and implement read()/write() functions.
- Imitate unitree_description to generate URDF files and maintain joint/link naming conventions.
- Only start real-time state estimation and legged_controller on real hardware.

## Effective fixes

- Isolate platform differences via ros-control hardware interface; separate simulation from hardware in official startup order.

## Result

- Official README lists multiple lab runs on A1 and provides historical records of 2 hours to 1 day; author's structure matches the repository.

## Limitations

- Repository is no longer maintained; version, dependencies, and safety boundaries must be re-verified against current fork.

## Safety notes

- Official README explicitly states that real hardware cannot start cheater controller; initial control should use cradle, low gain, limit, and emergency stop.

## Image and visual evidence

- The main framework diagram shows trajectory → NMPC → WBC → forward force torque + low gain PD, and IMU/actuator state → Kalman filter; the repository README text is consistent with this.

## Applicability boundary

- Applicable to the ROS1/ros-control framework; the repository is no longer maintained, and modern systems should evaluate migration costs.
